# opencode-web-bridges

## Use ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek & Meta AI inside OpenCode — no API key

Turn your existing ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek and Meta AI subscriptions into
OpenCode models. One install, no API key, no per-token billing.

![Demo](docs/demo-gemini.gif)

### What it does

- **No API key needed** — uses your already-logged-in browser session
- **Four engines** — ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek and Meta AI, side by side
- **One-line install** — `npx @bojackduy/opencode-web-bridges install`
- **Fail-closed recovery** — interrupted turns never re-submit
- **Checksum-verified** binaries for supply-chain safety
- **Open source** under AGPL-3.0

### Quick start

1. Install: `npx @bojackduy/opencode-web-bridges install`
2. Restart OpenCode, pick `chatgpt-web/chatgpt-web` in /models
3. Log in once with `/chatgpt-login`
4. Start coding

### Engines

| Engine | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT Web | Browser (CDP) | Full features: projects, threads, recovery |
| Gemini Web | Browser (CDP) | Text-only, local build, batch support |
| DeepSeek Web | HTTP+SSE | No browser needed, needs a token, tool calls |
| Meta AI Web | Browser (CDP) | Meta AI models via browser session |

### Prerequisites

Node.js 20+, OpenCode v1 or v2, Bun 1.1+, Chrome/Chromium.

### Support

Open an issue on GitHub. Include the adapter log stage and reason code.

# Changelog

## 0.1.2 — npm homepage points to landing page

- Set package `homepage` to the deployed landing page so npm links there instead of the repo README.

## Unreleased

- Add Node-compatible `npx @bojackduy/opencode-web-bridges install` launcher with v1/v2 host detection, explicit config/host selection and a no-side-effects dry-run.
- Preserve JSONC comments, options, manual config and disabled entries; prepare checksum-verified bridge binaries before backed-up atomic config edits.
- Check Bun/Chrome prerequisites read-only, leaving browser login and process supervision to the plugin after restart. Public use still requires npm publication and the first bridge GitHub release.

## 0.1.0 — Initial scaffold

- Hermetic login-command tests: no real Chrome launch or adapter probes during prepack.
- v1 first-install MCP registration waits for binary resolution instead of storing a placeholder command.
- CI and tag-driven npm trusted publishing with provenance; first publication remains manual.
- Host-specific install syntax documented for v1 (`plugin`) and v2 (`plugins`).
- One-line install: `plugin` array entry injects the `chatgpt-web` provider + `chatgpt` MCP via the `config` hook (fill-missing only, never clobbers).
- Managed binaries: downloads `chatgpt-openai` + `chatgpt-proxy` from GitHub releases into a versioned cache dir with sha256 verification.
- Supervisor: keeps the adapter listening and Chrome CDP answering while the plugin lives.
- Commands: `/chatgpt-status`, `/chatgpt-login`, `/chatgpt-doctor`.

---
description: Diagnose the ChatGPT Web bridge — binaries, ports, Chrome CDP, login state, each with repair hints.
---

Diagnose the ChatGPT Web bridge using the `chatgpt-doctor` tool.

Run the tool and present each PASS/FAIL line. For every FAIL, include its
repair hint verbatim and walk the user through the fix (re-download,
restart opencode, `/chatgpt-login`, log in once in the profile window).

---
description: Launch the profile Chrome window for one-time ChatGPT login, then re-probe readiness.
---

Log into the ChatGPT Web bridge using the `chatgpt-login` tool.

Run the tool: it launches Chrome with the dedicated profile and re-probes
the adapter. Tell the user to log into ChatGPT in that window ONCE — the
session persists in the profile dir and is reused forever. Then ask them to
re-run `/chatgpt-status` to confirm readiness.

---
description: Resolve this chat's unanswered turn — inspect what the bridge knows, read the previous reply back without resending, or deliberately clear the uncertainty.
---

Resolve this chat's unanswered turn using the `chatgpt-recover` tool.

Default to `action: "inspect"`: report what the state means, what is unknown,
what was kept, and which actions are available. Do not dump raw JSON and do
not mention endpoints, HTTP verbs or status codes in the summary.

If the report offers `recover`, run `action: "recover"` — it only reads the
previous reply back from the saved conversation; nothing is sent to ChatGPT
and no tool is run.

Only run `action: "abandon"` when the user explicitly asks to clear the chat,
and pass the chat id it names. Never pick the id for them, never clear a chat
that was not named, and always state that the cleared turn's historical tools
will not be re-run and that clearing is not proof the old reply arrived.

---
description: Show ChatGPT Web bridge status — readiness, login state, binary versions.
---

Show the ChatGPT Web bridge status using the `chatgpt-status` tool.

Run the tool and report its output. If it says NOT READY / not logged in,
tell the user to run `/chatgpt-login` (first run: log into ChatGPT once in
the profile Chrome window — the session persists in the profile).
